pr_title: Fix Sonos music library play problems
pr_body:
<!--

## Proposed change
Fixes problems with playing media from a sonos music library from the media browser and via service calls.

When browsing a sonos music library in the HA media browser, the media is presented in groups such as Artist, Composer, Genre; when selecting these the user is presented with a list of artists, composers or genres. Pressing the play button on any of these would play at most one album by the selected artist or sometimes play an album by a different artist if the name was the same (for example "Greatest Hits"), or play nothing.  This change fixes this behavior and allow playing media from any level in the browser.

The changes are to the handling of the play_media service call.  Hence, in addition to the media browser working properly, the service calls also now work properly and support the MediaPlayerEnqueue parameter (which was ignored.)

Note: This pull request currently includes changes from pull request #109518 which has not be merged yet; as these changes are required for this fix to work.

Service Call Examples include

Play all albums by the beatles
```
    - service: media_player.play_media
      target:
        entity_id: media_player.porch
      data:
        media_content_type: artist
        media_content_id: A:ALBUMARTIST/Beatles
```
Play all albums compose by Carlos Santana
```
    - service: media_player.play_media
      target:
        entity_id: media_player.porch
      data:
        media_content_type: composer
        media_content_id: A:COMPOSER/Carlos Santana
        enqueue: replace
```
Add an album to existing queue and play next
```
    - service: media_player.play_media
      target:
        entity_id: media_player.porch
      data:
        media_content_type: album
        media_content_id: A:ALBUM/Pump
        enqueue: next
```

issue_context.title: Sonos play artist only plays first album
issue_context.body:
### The problem

When in the media browser pressing play on an Artist only plays the first album by the artist rather than playing all albums by artist which is the expected behavior.  Likewise using a service call to play albums by an artist only plays the first album.

```
service: media_player.play_media
target:
  entity_id: media_player.sonos      
data:
  media_content_type: album
  media_content_id: A:ALBUMARTIST/Beatles
```

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2024-2-1

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

sonos

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/sonos/

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
service: media_player.play_media
target:
  entity_id: media_player.sonos      
data:
  media_content_type: album
  media_content_id: A:ALBUMARTIST/Beatles
```

_No response_

review_comments: This code to get the thumbnails did not work consistently with both the old implementation of get_media and the updated (in this pull request) implementation of get_media; because it was hard coding ALBUM_ARTIST as the search type. Instead look at the prefix and pick the right search type..

In theory, this block could end with `matches = [None]` which would end up returning `None` in the return statement below at line 541:
```python
    if len(matches) > 0:
        return matches[0]
```
It looks like this _shouldn't_ happen, but probably better to raise an error if it does come back empty.

You could do something like this:
```suggestion
            try:
                result = next((item for item in matches if (title == item.title)))
            except StopIteration as exc:
                raise BrowseError(f"Title '{title}' not found in results") from exc
            matches = [result]
```

The construct ends up working out, since matches =  [None] has len of 1 and then returning matches[0] then returns a None.  And the consumers handle the None.  I do agree it's not an ideal way to implement the logic and I can come up with something simpler.

I like the ideas of propagating an exception.  The the upstream code is not prepared for that right now and we'd want all branches in this function to do that.

For example, the code that gets the thumbnails does get None back when searching for track images (happens in the old implementation as well - I'm not sure why that happens yet, but its on my list) and it happily continues along (minus the track image showing in the media browser). An exception propagating would cause the browse to fail and the track list wouldn't be shown.

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/9580adfde90b04235bd338a45cf6c147286a2ae4/homeassistant/components/sonos/media_browser.py#L57-L62
